tasks.title: From Invisibility to Record: Women in American History
paras: During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, almost nothing was written about the contributions of women during the colonial period and the early history of the newly formed United States. Lacking the right to vote and absent from the seats of power, women were not considered an important force in history. Anne Bradstreet wrote some significant poetry in the seventeenth century, Mercy Otis Warren produced the best contemporary history of the American Revolution, and Abigail Adams penned important letters showing she exercised great political influence over her husband, John, the second President of the United States. But little or no notice was taken of these contributions. During these centuries, women remained invisible in history books. Throughout the nineteenth century, this lack of visibility continued, despite the efforts of female authors writing about women. These writers, like most of their male counterparts, were amateur historians. Their writings were celebratory in nature, and they were uncritical in their selection and use of sources.

During the nineteenth century, however, certain feminists showed a keen sense of history by keeping records of activities in which women were engaged. National, regional, and local women’s organizations compiled accounts of their doings. These sources form the core of the two greatest collections of women’s histories in the United States—one at the Elizabeth and Arthur Schlesinger Library at Radcliffe College, and the other the Sophia Smith Collection at Smith College. Despite the gathering of more information, most of the writing about women conformed to the “great women” theory of history. Most of these leaders were involved in public life as reformers, activists working for women’s right to vote, or authors.

questions.stem: What does the passage mainly discuss?

options.A: The role of literature in early American histories
options.B: The place of American women in written histories
options.C: The keen sense of history shown by American women
options.D: The “great women” approach to history used by American historians

questions.analysis: 题型：主旨题 原文定位： 第一段首句：“almost nothing was written about the contributions of women”，贯穿全文都在探讨女性在历史书写中的缺席与逐步被记录。 正确答案分析： 文章讨论的是女性在历史记录中的地位，从17–18世纪几乎不被记录，到19世纪女性开始自己保存历史，再到“great women”理论的批评。 选项分析： A. 文学在历史中的作用非主线，只涉及个别例子； C. 虽提及女性有“keen sense of history”，但非整篇主旨； D. “great women”理论仅为文末一部分。

questions.stem: The word “contemporary” in the text means that the history was
questions.analysis: 题型：词汇题 原文定位： “...Mercy Otis Warren produced the best contemporary history of the American Revolution...” 正确答案分析： “contemporary”在该语境下是指“当时的、同时代的”，不是“现代的”或“批判性的”。 选项分析： A informative（信息丰富）——语义不符； C thoughtful（深思的）——无关； D faultfinding（挑剔的）——语义错误。

questions.stem: According to the passage, Bradstreet, Warren, and Adams are mentioned to show that

options.A: a woman’s status was changed by marriage
options.B: even the contributions of outstanding women were ignored
options.C: only three women were able to get their writing published
options.D: poetry produced by women was more readily accepted than other writing by women

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文定位： 第一段：“But little or no notice was taken of these contributions.” 正确答案分析： 文中通过提及三位有成就的女性作家/思想者，说明她们的重要贡献被忽视，强调女性“invisible”。 选项分析： A 婚姻影响未涉及； C 并非仅三人能出版，而是举例说明； D 没有强调诗歌更受欢迎。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what weakness in nineteenth-century histories does the author point out?

options.A: They put too much emphasis on daily activities.
options.B: They left out discussion of the influence of money on politics.
options.C: The sources of the information they were based on were not necessarily accurate.
options.D: They were printed on poor-quality paper.

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文定位： 第一段末：“they were uncritical in their selection and use of sources.” 正确答案分析： 指出这些女性作家的历史写作缺乏批判性，对资料不严谨。 选项分析： A 太强调 daily activities ——文中没提； B 没有涉及金钱和政治； D 印刷质量未提及。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the author mentions all of the following as possible roles of nineteenth-century “great women” EXCEPT
questions.analysis: 题型：排除列举题 原文定位： 第二段末：“reformers, activists working for women’s right to vote, or authors.” 正确答案分析： 明确列出三种角色，未提及政治家（politicians），符合 EXCEPT 题型特点。 选项分析： A、B、C 均有提及； D 为正确答案，因为未出现于文中。
